title: MingCute Screenshot Quality Recovery batch 032
review_goal: Differentiate five MingCute cursor and finger variants with screenshot grounded depicts and deterministic evidence fields.

items.depicts_observation: Solid pointer arrow outline leaning slightly left with a thick lower tail
items.context_bias: Use when the interface wants a simple pointer arrow without click sparks or open center lines.
items.ambiguity_note: Do not use for the open arrow or click pointer when the thick solid arrow body matters.
items.selection_reason: The screenshot shows the fullest triangular pointer shape with a thick lower tail segment.

items.depicts_observation: Open pointer arrow outline leaning right with a separated lower tail line
items.context_bias: Use when the interface wants a lighter open pointer shape instead of a solid triangular arrow.
items.ambiguity_note: Do not use for the solid pointer when the open center and separated tail are visible.
items.selection_reason: The screenshot opens the arrow center and detaches the lower tail into a separate line.

items.depicts_observation: Pointer arrow outline with four short click rays at the upper left
items.context_bias: Use when the interface wants a cursor icon that explicitly shows a click or tap burst.
items.ambiguity_note: Do not use for the plain pointer arrows when the short click rays are part of the visual.
items.selection_reason: The screenshot adds four short click rays around the pointer tip area.

items.depicts_observation: Rounded hand outline with one raised index finger and a closed palm loop
items.context_bias: Use when the interface wants a touch hand icon built as one rounded palm loop and one raised finger.
items.ambiguity_note: Do not use for the detailed finger hand when the palm should stay as one simple loop.
items.selection_reason: The screenshot shows a rounded palm loop with one straight raised finger and no extra finger detail.

items.depicts_observation: Hand outline with one raised index finger and several curved finger bumps
items.context_bias: Use when the interface wants the raised finger hand that also shows the other curled finger bumps.
items.ambiguity_note: Do not use for the simpler looped palm hand when the extra finger bumps need to remain visible.
items.selection_reason: The screenshot adds multiple curved finger bumps along the right side of the hand.
